method: Web text search and image search before generation; official collection descriptions checked. Image references inform the concept; no remote image file copied to the mod or submitted to imagegen.

sources.supports: Navy Board order in 1716 accompanied new designs/repairs with scale models; model use in design review.
Eighteenth-century design/model complexity; does not establish exact date for the proposed icon.

references.interpretation: Unrigged complete hull model plus divider; simplified generic reconstruction. Not the previously approved diagonal-framing fragment or finished iron hull.

sources.supports: Society originated in 1760; Register Book from 1764 funds surveyors to list, rate and class ships.
Digitised original 1764-66 register. Search excerpt read; direct open returned 403.
Early hull/equipment assessments and A1 by 1775/76.

references.interpretation: Symbolic open register, no copied company logo or cover, no fake text. Ship diagram and caliper are semantic devices, not features claimed for the original register.

sources.supports: Contemporary model of Greathead boat: double-ended clinker hull, strong sheer, internal and exterior cork buoyancy; 1790-1810.
Early lifesaving boats and Greathead design circa 1790; rowing and cork protection.

references.interpretation: Simplified early rescue boat, two stored oars for icon legibility; not the complete operating crew/oar complement. No later plastic lifebuoy or RNLI logo.

observations: Screw frigate is a volumetric ship with spars, useful style but too finished/later for the design concept.
Power of the purse is a spilled coin bag, unrelated to naval condition assessment.
Navigation is chart/compass/divider; correct travel theme but not lifesaving. New subjects must not repeat this chart.
